title: PAL: A Variability-Aware Policy for Scheduling ML Workloads in GPU Clusters
problem: GPU clusters experience performance variability across accelerators that causes resource under-utilization and load imbalance when scheduling concurrent ML jobs. Existing cluster schedulers do not account for application-specific susceptibility to this variability.
motivation: Optimizing GPU-rich clusters for ML and scientific computing applications is critical as accelerator usage grows for ML workloads.
method: PAL uses performance variability measurements and application-specific profiles to make job placement decisions. It characterizes which applications are more susceptible to variability and balances this awareness with locality constraints to minimize nodes used while mitigating variability effects.
key_novelty: Explicitly characterizing application-specific performance variability profiles and incorporating that information into job placement decisions for cluster scheduling.
contributions: Characterization framework identifying applications susceptible to performance variability in GPU clusters
PAL scheduler design using variability profiles and locality balancing for improved job placement
Demonstrates 42% geomean job completion time improvement and 47% makespan reduction over state-of-the-art schedulers
primary_theme: variability-aware GPU cluster scheduling for ML workloads
